- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.16 → 81.91) are common, suggesting model fails to account for post-spike mean reversion or policy-induced volatility.
- Model underestimates late-period price increases, particularly in the final 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10 days, with diminishing error as forecast horizon progresses.
- Model exhibits “lagged” behavior — it reacts to recent price movements but underestimates the magnitude of subsequent moves.
- When history includes a recent spike, model often overcorrects downward, then fails to recover fully.
- Model does not adequately capture the “tail risk” or policy-driven price surges in the final 5–7 days of the forecast.
